attempts.summary: Built an Ansible-driven VRRP failover gateway for node3 to reach node4 across the two VyOS routers (node1/node2), using node5 as the Ansible control node. node3 and node4 sit on separate private segments (10.10.10.0/24 and 10.10.20.0/24) that only node1/node2 bridge; each router now runs two VRRP groups (NET-A-GW vrid 10 on eth1, NET-B-GW vrid 20 on eth2) with node1 priority 200 (preferred master) and node2 priority 100 (backup, preempt enabled). node3's single gateway for reaching node4 is the VRRP VIP 10.10.10.254 (route 10.10.20.0/24 via that VIP); node4 symmetrically routes back via 10.10.20.254, so both directions survive either router going down. Verified with a live failover test (stopped keepalived on node1, confirmed node2 became MASTER on both groups with zero ping loss to node4, then restored node1 and confirmed it preempted back to MASTER). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: rebooted node3, node4, node5, node1, and node2 one at a time (native `reboot`, backgrounded so the ack returned first), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed post-restart recovery (Alpine static IP/route persisted via /etc/network/interfaces; VyOS VRRP/config persisted via `save`, node1 re-preempted to MASTER, node2 returned to BACKUP, node5's Ansible project and cluster SSH key intact) before moving to the next node, preserving VRRP quorum throughout.
